approaches.name: qrexec-client-vm adapter plus read-only authenticated probe
approaches.why: Uses the production VM-to-VM qrexec client boundary and existing framed protocol while proving transport, authentication, persistent counters, timeout handling, policy-denial propagation, and pending-request reconciliation without mutating mission state.

approaches.name: jump directly to synthetic claim mutation over real qrexec
approaches.why: Closer to final behavior but unnecessarily changes coordinator mission state before the transport/auth boundary itself is proven in a real Qube.

approaches.name: HTTP or socket acceptance proxy
approaches.why: Exercises a different trust and transport boundary and introduces a network/socket surface not used by the selected qrexec design.

approaches.name: process-boundary stdio simulation only
approaches.why: Excellent deterministic CI coverage but cannot validate Qubes policy evaluation, qrexec-client-vm invocation, or a real VM boundary.

failuresAndLessons: Treat qrexec process timeout and policy denial as explicit fail-closed errors rather than transport retries.
Bound stdout and stderr collection so a faulty remote service cannot grow worker memory without limit.
Validate target/service names before spawn and never invoke through a shell.
Use a read-only request-status probe as the first real-Qubes acceptance gate; synthetic mission mutation is the next gate only after this succeeds.
A green fake-qrexec CI test is not evidence of a real Qubes deployment. REAL-WORKER readiness still requires execution inside isolated Qubes with installed policy/service.
